questions.query: Compare Apple's Legal Proceedings (Item 3) across its FY2022 and FY2025 10-Ks.
questions.gold_answer: The two years differ substantially in scope. FY2022's cited Item 3 text covers two topics: ‘Epic Games’ (the district court ruled for Apple on 9 of 10 counts and on Apple's breach-of-contract counterclaim on September 10, 2021, found certain App Store Review Guidelines provisions violated California's unfair competition law and issued an injunction; Epic appealed and Apple cross-appealed, with a stay granted) and ‘Other Legal Proceedings’ (routine ordinary-course matters). FY2025's cited Item 3 text covers two additional topics not present in FY2022's cited text: ‘Digital Markets Act Investigations’ (the EU Commission opened Article 5(4) and Article 6(4) investigations in 2024, fined Apple €500 million in the Article 5(4) matter in April 2025 and issued a cease-and-desist order, which Apple has appealed) and ‘Department of Justice Lawsuit’ (DOJ and state attorneys general filed a civil antitrust suit in the District of New Jersey on March 21, 2024 alleging monopolization in smartphone markets). The ‘Epic Games’ entry is also substantially further developed in FY2025's cited text: the California District Court found Apple in violation of the 2021 Injunction on April 30, 2025, barred commissions/fees on outside-app purchases, denied Apple's motion to narrow the injunction, referred the matter for a possible criminal contempt determination, and Apple has appealed to the Ninth Circuit.

questions.query: What risks related to intellectual property litigation does Alphabet disclose in its FY2023 10-K?
questions.gold_answer: Alphabet discloses that, like other internet, technology, and media companies, it is frequently subject to litigation alleging infringement or other violations of intellectual property rights, including patent, copyright, trade secrets, and trademarks. Parties have sought broad injunctive relief against Alphabet in U.S. and international courts and the U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC), seeking exclusion and cease-and-desist orders, and patent-holding companies frequently seek to generate income from patents by bringing claims against Alphabet; the number of such claims has increased as the business has expanded. Separately, Alphabet also discloses an AI-specific patent risk: other companies may hold or obtain patents or other proprietary rights that could prevent, limit, or interfere with Alphabet's ability to make, use, or sell its own AI products and services.

questions.query: What macroeconomic and geopolitical risks does Microsoft disclose in its FY2023 10-K?
questions.gold_answer: Microsoft discloses that abrupt political change, terrorist activity, and armed conflict — such as the ongoing conflict in Ukraine — pose a risk of general economic disruption in affected countries, which may increase operating costs and negatively affect the Company's ability to sell to and collect from customers in those markets, and may add uncertainty to customers' technology-investment timing and budgets. Separately, it discloses that worsening economic conditions — including inflation, recession, pandemic, or other changes — may cause lower IT spending and adversely affect revenue, including through declining demand for PCs, servers, and other computing devices.
